On Canada, Panama, Iran, and China - an exploration of the power architecture of water, strategic energy dependency, and the military hierarchy hiding underneath our understanding of shared geography. | | | Oct 3 | | | | | | | | | | | | For most of my lifetime, the people on either side of the Canada-US border had the luxury of forgetting the geography between them. Families went shopping or visited friends on either side of the border on a weekend whim. The border was a line on a road map. NORAD was background architecture. Pipelines were infrastructure, the Arctic was white space at the top of a schoolroom map, and the strait that separates Vancouver Island from Washington was gorgeous scenery from a ferry deck. That luxury rested on a political assumption: however much our two countries disagreed, neither would deliberately turn the other 's dependence into a weapon. That assumption has weakened. And Canada has noticed. Let's talk about where this might be going, and what history can teach us about what happens when chokepoints become leverage, and alliances become competition. | | ---|---|--- Canada has discovered that interdependence can become leverage Two wealthy democracies built integrated auto plants, shared electricity grids, ran pipelines and railroads across the border, and let families cross back and forth for generations. The integration went so deep that we stopped seeing it as a vulnerability. Then Trump began musing about a fifty-first state while using tariffs and market access as instruments of pressure. Canada 's answer has not been submission. It has been diversification, and its prime minister has been unusually candid about why. In August, Mark Carney said his government had recognized that America had changed: that Washington would impose tariffs on close allies and "use economic integration as a weapon." His government, he said, would pursue an agreement with the United States, but not "at any price," and not at the expense of Canadian sovereignty. That candor has now become policy. Ottawa says Canadian exports to non-U.S. markets are on track to double over the next decade. It is expanding trade corridors and port capacity, pursuing agreements from India and ASEAN to the Gulf and Europe, and treating energy as what Carney has called a key lever for Canadian "prosperity, resilience and independence." And just today, the partners in LNG Canada approved a second phase of the Kitimat project that is expected to double its production capacity to 28 million tonnes a year. Canada is not talking about independence in the abstract. It is physically rebuilding its economy around it. But sovereignty has layers. There is resource sovereignty : we own the oil. There is market sovereignty : we decide whom we sell it to. And there is corridor sovereignty : we can actually reach those buyers without another power 's permission. Canada unquestionably possesses the first. It is deliberately expanding the second. The third is where geography begins arguing back. You can diversify your customers and your currency exposure. You can build another pipeline. You cannot move Vancouver Island. The geography underneath the economy The scale of the dependency is what makes the story interesting. In 2025, Canada supplied 63.4% of all U.S. crude-oil imports. At the same time, roughly 90% of Canada's crude exports still went to the United States, amounting to about 3.9 million barrels per day. Those are not identical vulnerabilities. Canada depends heavily on one customer; the United States depends heavily on one foreign supplier. But they are extraordinarily concentrated and mutually consequential vulnerabilities. The expanded Trans Mountain pipeline was built in large part to loosen Canada's dependence on the American market. Its roughly 890,000-barrel-per-day capacity allows Alberta crude to reach the Pacific at Burnaby and increasingly move toward Asian markets rather than flowing almost automatically south. Economically, yes, that is diversification. Geographically, every tanker departing Burnaby enters the Salish Sea and eventually reaches the Pacific through the Strait of Juan de Fuca at the very farthest northwest corner of the United States -- the narrow waterway between Vancouver Island and Washington State. I live in Washington. That waterway is part of the landscape of the Pacific Northwest, one I've enjoyed, crossed, driven beside dozens of times -- and it runs beside (nuclear-capable submarine station) Bangor Subase, Bremerton Naval Shipyard, Whidbey Island Naval Airbase, and Joint Base Lewis-McCord (Air Force/Army) -- one of the densest concentrations of American military infrastructure on the continent. Let me be precise about what that does and does not mean. It does not mean the United States can legally close the strait whenever it likes. Navigation rights, bilateral arrangements, Canadian sovereignty, alliance commitments and the consequences of armed interference all matter enormously. The two countries even operate a cooperative vessel-traffic system there. But physical geography exists beneath legal geography. And history keeps teaching one stubborn lesson: A trade route can be legally international, commercially indispensable and politically normalized right up until a crisis makes someone notice who can physically control it. The immediate argument comes from a recent opinion piece by Larry Hughes of Dalhousie University, and I want to credit it while disagreeing with some of its theater. Hughes asks what happens when a country diversifies its buyers but cannot diversify its geography. That is the right question. His scenarios of American warships turning Canadian tankers around are a much bigger leap, and I don't think the available evidence supports them. I want to take the question seriously without borrowing the panic. Because history offers plenty to think about without inventing a blockade. Suez: when an ally discovers the hierarchy In 1956, Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company. Britain and France considered the canal strategically indispensable, and together with Israel, secretly coordinated military action. Israel invaded Sinai. British and French forces followed, ostensibly to separate the belligerents and secure the waterway. Then something extraordinary happened. The United States turned its leverage not against Egypt, but against its own allies. Washington opposed the invasion and pressured London and Paris to withdraw. Meanwhile, the closure of the canal and related pipelines produced severe energy shortages. British and French officials told DC that oil supplies had fallen 25 to 30 percent below normal requirements and accused the United States of withholding emergency oil cooperation in order to increase pressure for withdrawal. Suez is often told as the story of a canal. It is better understood as the story of a hierarchy. Britain was still an empire, still a major military power and still one of America's closest allies. Yet it discovered that its freedom of action was constrained by the financial, logistical and energy systems surrounding it. Power is not just possession. It is freedom of maneuver inside systems of dependency. Panama: when a superpower helped redraw the map around a corridor If Suez shows an imperial power discovering the limits of its freedom around a waterway, Panama shows a rising power reorganizing geography around one. At the beginning of the twentieth century, Washington wanted an interoceanic canal. When Colombia 's congress rejected the proposed canal treaty in 1903, Theodore Roosevelt dispatched American warshipsto Panama City and Col on in support of Panamanian independence. The newly established Republic of Panama then granted the United States control over a ten-mile-wide Canal Zone. The arrangement lasted for most of the twentieth century. The canal shortened naval deployments between oceans. It shortened commercial routes. It altered the strategic geography of the United States itself. Even the later treaties that transferred the canal back to Panama preserved special provisions regarding its permanent neutrality and defense. Panama assumed full control in 1999. The American century was built partly on an insight most civilians rarely have reason to consider: Water has architecture. Certain stretches of it matter more than others. And whoever can reliably control access through them acquires power wildly disproportionate to their physical size. Hormuz: from shipping lane to "vital interest" In January 1980, following the Iranian Revolution and the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, President Jimmy Carter made the principle explicit: An attempt by an outside power to gain control of the Persian Gulf region, he declared, would be regarded as an assault on the "vital interests" of the United States and could be repelled by military force. The Persian Gulf did not belong to America. But its energy flows sat inside an economic and security architecture Washington regarded as vital, and internal U.S. strategic documents were candid about protecting those interests. During the Iran-Iraq Tanker War a few years later, the principle became operational. Beginning in 1987, Operation Earnest Will put U.S. Navy escorts around reflagged Kuwaiti tankers transiting the Gulf. It became the largest American naval convoy operation since the Second World War. So the pattern has several faces. At Suez, imperial powers attempted to seize a corridor. At Panama, a rising power helped reshape political geography around one. At Hormuz, a superpower declared another region's strategic corridor important enough to defend by force. The contexts are very different. The underlying recognition is not: Chokepoints are power. We are watching that principle operate again in real time. Before the current war with Iran, the Strait of Hormuz carried roughly 20.9 million barrels of petroleum per day--about one-fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption--along with enormous LNG volumes. Before the war, roughly 125 large commercial vessels typically crossed the strait each day. On September 23, tracking data counted only tencommodity-vessel transits. People thousands of miles away are rediscovering that geography is real. Diesel prices. Insurance premiums. Governments opening strategic reserves. Washington announced today that it will offer to loan up to 40 million additional barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve as part of the international response to the disruption. For decades, Americans could treat maritime chokepoints as something found on a slide in a Pentagon briefing. In 2026, Hormuz is something Americans find in the price of diesel at the pump every Tuesday. Bab el-Mandeb: the chokepoint behind the chokepoint Diversification can also relocate vulnerability rather than eliminate it. Saudi Arabia built its East-West pipeline partly to reduce dependence on shipping through Hormuz. The pipeline terminates at Yanbu on the Red Sea. That means bypassing one chokepoint increases the importance of another: the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow southern entrance to the Red Sea. When Houthi attacks made the route increasingly dangerous beginning in late 2023, oil flows through Bab el-Mandeb fell from roughly 8.7 million barrels per day in 2023 to around 4 million per day through the first eight months of 2024. Meanwhile, traffic rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope surged - an entire circumnavigation of the continent of Africa, adding many days per trip and dramatically increasing transit costs, all to avoid a war zone that didn't have to be one. The current Iran conflict has exposed the same problem again. Saudi Arabia has pushed more crude westward through the East-West system while Red Sea security and shipping risk remain part of the calculation. This is the systems lesson: Resilience is not achieved simply by building an alternate route. You have to ask what the alternate route depends on. The Trans Mountain expansion reduces one Canadian dependency. It does not abolish geography. Greenland, the Arctic, and the top edge of the map Greenland is not another Hormuz. Nobody can turn an oil valve there. It belongs in this story because the Arctic is becoming increasingly important as a strategic maritime space: for military access, surveillance, shipping, critical minerals and the movement of forces between the Arctic and North Atlantic. This month, after years of extraordinary tension over American ambitions toward Greenland, the United States, Denmark and Greenland reached a new security agreement expanding American military access while reaffirming Greenlandic self-determination. But the more directly relevant Canadian example sits farther west. Canada considers the waterways of the Northwest Passage to be Canadian internal waters. The United States considers the passage a strait used for international navigation, through which foreign vessels possess transit rights. The disagreement has been managed peacefully for decades, including through a 1988 cooperation agreement. But the legal disagreement itself remains. That makes the Northwest Passage a remarkably useful case study. Two of the closest allies on Earth can cooperate extensively and still disagree about a fundamental question: Who ultimately governs strategically important water? For decades, the answer to that question could remain politely unresolved because the stakes were limited. But now, as Arctic access grows more economically and strategically consequential, those tactful ambiguities become distinctly less secure. Sanctions, the Caribbean, and chokepoints that aren't made of rock Not every corridor is geographic. The Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico have long formed part of Washington's strategic perimeter, and energy provides a particularly useful example of how power over flows can be exercised without physically stopping a ship. When the United States sanctions an oil-producing country such as Venezuela, the pressure does not have to begin with a deployed destroyer. It can operate through banks. Insurers. Shipping companies. Refiners. Payment systems. Port access. Foreign buyers deciding whether doing business with the sanctioned country is worth risking their own access to the American market. You do not necessarily have to stop the tanker if you can make the insurer, bank, refiner or purchaser unwilling or legally unable to touch its cargo. The distinction is helpful because sanctions, secondary sanctions and physical maritime interdiction are legally and strategically different instruments. But from a systems perspective they can attack the same vulnerability: the corridor between possession and exchange. Cuba offers an unusually stark current example. Reuters now describes a U.S.-imposed oil blockade as worsening severe Cuban fuel shortages and contributing to the country's broader energy crisis. Some chokepoints are straits. Others are financial, legal or technological. Great-power leverage becomes especially formidable when those systems overlap. Juan de Fuca is not Hormuz To be clear: Canada is not Iran. The United States and Canada are treaty allies with extraordinarily integrated militaries and economies. Commercial shipping enjoys navigation rights that cannot simply be erased because Washington dislikes Canadian policy. A unilateral American attempt to physically interdict Canadian exports would be an extraordinary escalation, far beyond tariffs. It would raise grave questions under international law and reverberate through NATO, NORAD, financial markets and the entire architecture of the North American relationship. There is no evidence so far that anyone in DC is preparing to do that. The reason to look at the vulnerability anyway is that the time to understand a chokepoint is before a crisis. Every chokepoint looks benign while everyone agrees about how it should function. Just like every implicit contract looks benevolent when everyone's still friends. And blockade is hardly the only form coercion can take. Between ordinary trade policy and naval interdiction lies a wide middle--the terrain where modern great powers usually prefer to operate. Depending on the country and legal regime, pressure can take the form of sanctions, insurance restrictions, port-access rules, customs enforcement, tanker blacklists, export controls, security inspections, secondary sanctions on foreign buyers, financial restrictions or pressure on shipping companies. Those tools are not identical. Nor has the United States used every one against every target. The point is that physical interdiction sits at the extreme end of a much larger spectrum of leverage. Most of that spectrum is quieter, more technical and more incremental. And it is often where dependency becomes politically consequential. Four days ago, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said DC saw little urgency in resolving the escalating trade dispute with Canada, even as new restrictions and major sectoral tariffs loom and Canada retaliates. That does not yet signal a maritime confrontation. It signals something less theatrical and perhaps more important: the political assumption under which these shared systems were built has changed. The paradox: coercion teaches exits There is a recurring paradox in international politics. Coercion can produce exactly the strategic behavior it was intended to prevent. Every time dependence becomes leverage, the dependent state receives an incentive to make itself harder to coerce. That is precisely what Ottawa now says it is doing. More Pacific export capacity, LNG, trade relationships, port infrastructure, internal investment, Arctic capability. More effort to reach Europe and Asia without treating American market access as the automatic destination for Canadian production. Carney's government describes the strategy explicitly as moving from reliance toward resilience and says non-U.S. exports are on track to double over the coming decade. Great powers have repeatedly discovered that coercive pressure teaches other states to build exits. Europe learned the lesson painfully from dependence on Russian gas. Saudi Arabia built infrastructure to bypass Hormuz. And perhaps the most revealing comparison comes from China. The Malacca dilemma China has spent decades confronting its own version of the corridor problem. Its economy became deeply dependent on imported energy arriving by sea. A huge share of those supplies crossed the Strait of Malacca, the narrow passage between the Malay Peninsula and Indonesia connecting the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Chinese strategists came to worry about what became known as the Malacca dilemma : in a major-power confrontation, China's access to essential energy could be vulnerable to naval forces it did not control. The Council on Foreign Relations summarizes the strategic concern starkly: as the world's largest energy importer, China has worried that U.S. forces could blockade Malacca during a conflict and interrupt much of its energy supply. Chinese port investments, alternative overland corridors and projects such as the route through Pakistan can therefore be understood partly as attempts to reduce exposure to that vulnerability. That concern helps explain the appeal of pipelines from Russia and Central Asia, overland links through Myanmar and Pakistan, overseas port access, strategic reserves and a navy increasingly capable of sustained operations far from China's home waters. Canada and China are obviously not analogous political systems. DC is not - so far as we know - preparing to strangle Canadian shipping. But structurally, the realization is recognizable. A country can possess enormous resources. It can possess enormous economic capacity. It can sign trade agreements across the world. And still discover that the road between producer and consumer passes through geography it does not completely control. None of these conflicts happened because geography changed. It happened because trust did. Independence creates its own security dilemma There is another side to the story, and it belongs to Canada. As a country builds alternative corridors, those corridors become more valuable. Trans Mountain, Vancouver, Kitimat, Arctic ports, critical-mineral routes, all start to matter more. And therefore protecting them becomes more important. Canada has barely had to think about some of these questions during the long era of comfortable continental integration. Who protects Canadian shipping? How much naval capacity does meaningful autonomy require? How many icebreakers? How much Arctic surveillance? Which ports require redundancy? Which supply chains should be duplicated? How much refining and processing should happen domestically rather than exporting raw resources? How much infrastructure should exist simply so that Canada retains choices it may rarely need to exercise? This is one of the uncomfortable costs of resilience. Efficiency rewards concentration. Resilience rewards redundancy. Extra ports, pipelines, inventories, factories, ships and alternate routes can look wasteful when systems are functioning normally. Their value appears when normal stops being guaranteed. That leads to the hardest question so far: If your security architecture is supplied in large part by the same superpower from which you are trying to become less dependent,how independent can you actually be? Suez offers a final warning here. Britain and the United States were allies in 1956, but that did not make their interests identical. Washington concluded that the Anglo-French operation threatened broader American interests and used its superior economic and logistical leverage against its friends. The alliance survived; the hierarchy inside it was exposed. Canadians and Americans can remain friends. NORAD can continue. NATO can continue. Hundreds of billions of dollars in commerce can continue. Families can keep crossing the border. None of that guarantees permanent geopolitical alignment. Carney's stated strategy is not rupture with America. It is a refusal to make Canadian sovereignty contingent entirely on American goodwill. In August, he described the government's objectives as maintaining Canada's "flexibility, independence, and sovereignty" while acknowledging that the old relationship with the United States is not coming back. That strategy may ultimately make the relationship more stable. But transitions from dependency to resilience can themselves create... friction. Especially when the more powerful partner exhibits a strategic and psychological tendency towards coercive control. Sovereignty is partly the ability to say no Canada is doing what states have repeatedly done when dependence begins to feel dangerous. It is building exits. New customers. New ports. New pipelines. New alliances. New industries. It can choose where it sells its oil. It can choose who buys its gas. It can decide how much refining capacity to build at home and which relationships to cultivate abroad. It can decide how much redundancy it is willing to pay for. But the three layers of sovereignty remain stubbornly different. Resource sovereignty: we own it. Market sovereignty: we decide where it goes. Corridor sovereignty: we can actually get it there. Venezuela demonstrates how financial architecture can constrain the second. Hormuz demonstrates vulnerability in the third. Panama shows what direct control of a corridor can mean. Suez shows how abruptly access, energy, finance and alliance hierarchy can intersect. Bab el-Mandeb shows that rerouting can simply move the vulnerability somewhere else. Malacca shows what happens when a major state recognizes the problem and spends decades trying to engineer around it. Canada is now deliberately expanding its market sovereignty while discovering that corridor sovereignty is harder. It can choose where it sells its resources. It can choose how much independence it is willing to pay for. It cannot choose its geography, or its neighbor. And somewhere between Burnaby and the open Pacific, in water close enough to feel like part of my own landscape, long-presumed neutral cooperation is fast becoming a real and serious question. Can you believe it? We're officially 31 days away from Election Day! Before I share why this month is hands down the _most important and consequential month of the campaign_ , I want to take a moment to look back at where this all started -- and how far we've come together.
### Where it all started
It all began with a simple idea: Kansans deserve a senator who actually listens to them. I never quite thought that I would run to become that senator. After all, I'm a pastor, not a politician.
But I decided to step up because I saw just how badly Washington's chaos -- and cruelty -- was hurting the neighbors I love and the communities I serve.
I'll be honest: I didn't know exactly what to expect from a Senate race. But we hit the ground running and have come so incredibly far, all thanks to supporters like you.
### Where we are, one month before Election Day
With 31 days until the big day, let me give you the lay of the land:
* The newest polls show us running neck and neck with Sen. Marshall -- with some even giving us a narrow lead.
* Over the past several weeks, election experts have shifted our race _further away_ from a "Safe Republican" rating, with RealClearPolling even calling Kansas a 50/50 TOSS-UP. _These shifts confirm that this race is going to be very close._
* The Senate Leadership Fund -- a major GOP super PAC -- just announced they're launching a $15 million ad buy to attack me.

These aren't just numbers; they are proof that Kansas is ready for change.
When I look at these metrics -- which all point to this being one of the most competitive races in the nation -- I am filled with gratitude for folks like you. The truth is, no one expected Kansas to become a battleground. It's only because of this grassroots team that we're on the brink of making history.
Whether you phone-banked or knocked on doors or chipped in a few bucks or even just shared one of these posts with a friend, you are the reason our momentum is surging.
**Please don 't forget this: All the good we do in Washington will be thanks to you. That's something to be immensely proud of. **
### Roger Marshall's recent months:
Roger Marshall's deep ties to Florida were further exposed.
"Reporting by the Kansas City Star revealed Marshall took official trips from Washington, D.C., to Sarasota, spending more than $18,000 in taxpayer funds from 2021 to 2024. The trips reportedly stopped after a hurricane destroyed the area. It is unlawful for a senator to use taxpayer money for personal travel."
There was an embarrassing rejection by voters at the Kansas State Fair debate on his "home turf."
It's clear Kansans are ready for a new voice in Washington.
### It all comes down to this final month
But right now, we find ourselves at a critical juncture. In a 50/50 toss-up race, it's anyone's game. It's these last weeks that will determine who pulls ahead and whose momentum slips.
That's why we're gearing up, not slowing down. We're preparing to air ads across Kansas to reach the final persuadable voters. We're building a massive get-out-the-vote effort to ensure all of our voters have a plan to get to the ballot box.
But here is our biggest challenge: Sen. Marshall's super PAC allies have already spent $7 million to crush our momentum, and they are gearing up to spend even more. The truth is that even our incredible momentum cannot withstand an attack this big without additional support. We need to fight back.
Here's a little window into our campaign: Every single day, we make tough decisions on how much we can spend to reach voters based on the amount of support we receive from folks like you. **[That's why I'm asking you to make a donation today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0b06051b-596b-4a8d-b0e1-efb460173ffe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
With the stakes so incredibly high in this _make-or-break month_ , we truly need everyone to take an active role in this movement, in all the ways you're able.
### So here are a few ways you can step up today:
1. **Endorse our campaign:** Join the tens of thousands of supporters who are already all in by endorsing me for Senate. Your support is the foundation -- and heart -- of this movement, and **[I'd be honored to have you with me](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0270f356-57e1-4921-9330-db7773d4101b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
2. **Volunteer with us:** Check out our volunteer opportunities **[here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3206a486-27ff-4e58-a4ae-afad1a9fe423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Whether it's knocking on doors, phone-banking or writing notes to Kansas voters, we need all hands on deck.
3. **Chip in to fuel our final sprint:** **[Finally, if you're able to contribute a few bucks today, it will make a massive difference at this critical moment in our campaign](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0b06051b-596b-4a8d-b0e1-efb460173ffe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
4. **Join us on social:** Get the latest campaign updates (plus photos and videos!) and share your thoughts with us on **[Facebook](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/66370606-d393-4936-ac6c-ded83dd672a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) , [Twitter](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/60f2f7d0-9765-46b7-817b-0ef815a39cac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Instagram](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3bd9227b-b25f-4e06-b7cb-e41e45fa775f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

The incredible truth is that on Nov. 3, we've got our best chance at making history in Kansas and giving working folks a champion in the Senate. It all rides on this final month. Thank you for being with me until the very end.
Yours,
Adam Hamilton

That took some serious _chutzpah_. My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind. That promise came true for him, and for generations of my family. That’s what sets America apart. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed. In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms. In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them. In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous. In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened. In 2026, I’m the Democratic nominee for VA-02, because Jen Kiggans either _can’t or won’t_ protect them. The fact is that Hampton Roads is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It's time for a leader with _chutzpah_.** VA-02 is rated a Toss-Up, and Trump and his friends have already poured over $5 million into this district to defeat me. This will be one of the toughest, costliest fights of the entire 2026 election cycle. **Luckily,_chutzpah_ runs in my family, and I’m not afraid of a little mishigas. **With you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need. body:
Derek, we know you hear from us pretty often, but this is important.
---
Derek, this is an email from the National Democratic Committee about our work to flip Congress in 31 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9619%2E22930333%2EZ-KaCl). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=2&akid=9619%2E22930333%2EZ-KaCl) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=9619%2E22930333%2EZ-KaCl), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=4&akid=9619%2E22930333%2EZ-KaCl). Derek, we know you hear from us pretty often. Emails, texts, ads, mail, it can be a lot. Here’s the deal: **We’re exactly one month out from Election Day.** That means we only have one month to reach every voter, knock every door, make every call. Every single day, for the next 31 days,_we need to leave it all on the field._ We want you to know that we don’t expect anyone to donate to _every_ email we send. But we depend on people like you chipping in what they can, when they can to fund our work because **over 99%** of the DNC’s contributions come from supporters like you. **So every single donation matters. Not because one donation changes everything, but because when thousands of contributions pile up, they have the power to change _anything_.** Over **one million people** have chipped in to power this movement to victory in the midterms this year. If you’re one of them: _thank you_. [**If you haven’t chipped in yet, and you’ve been waiting for the right time,_this is it_.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-october-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20261003_9619_fr&refcode2=9619_22930333_Z-KaCl&akid=9619%2E22930333%2EZ-KaCl) We’re running out of time — and every single dollar helps us expand our midterm operation. subject: This Democrat can win in Kansas
body:
Peter, I’m reaching out with an urgent request.
|
#
| | | | | Hi, Peter – Roy Cooper here. My friend Adam Hamilton is running for U.S. Senate over in Kansas, and he needs our support. If you can, [_I hope you'll split a donation between our grassroots campaigns._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19681?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1607&amount=5&t=7&akid=4185%2E124072%2EoO5dkB)

---|---
Peter, I’m reaching out with an urgent request.
A brand-new New York Times/Siena poll out this morning shows Adam Hamilton tied 45-45 with his Republican opponent in the Kansas U.S. Senate race. We can flip this seat blue.
**That’s why the GOP is panicking. Their top super PAC just launched a MASSIVE $15 million ad buy in Kansas to turn the tide against Adam and boost his opponent. He needs our immediate grassroots support to fight back.**
[**_You’ve stood by my side while I’ve faced these kinds of attacks. Now, I’m asking you to show up for Adam. Will you make a split donation of $5 between my campaign and Adam Hamilton’s right now? Flipping this seat – and the Senate – is crucial to getting our country back on the right track._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19681?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1607&amount=5&t=9&akid=4185%2E124072%2EoO5dkB)

Adam has been a pastor for the past 36 years, and he’s a fifth-generation Kansan.
He’s been called to run for Senate for many of the same reasons I have: He loves his home state. He cares deeply about the future of our country. He knows that Washington DC’s chaos and corruption are making life harder for folks, and he’s ready to fix things.
With experts at RealClearPolitics calling this race a “Toss Up” and the polls continuing to shift in his direction, Adam has what it takes to flip Kansas for the first time in nearly a _century._
**But not without your support – right here, right now. He’s getting outspent by the GOP, and he simply cannot fight back without you.[_Will you split $5 to help Adam and me flip our respective seats this November and build a brighter future for all?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19681?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1607&amount=5&t=14&akid=4185%2E124072%2EoO5dkB)**

Roy Cooper

| | Dear Friend who has common sense,I'm always going to stand with America.I'm always going to reject the extremes. I'm always going to reject Socialism.I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to...Abolish our bordersAbolish the electoral collegeAbolish IsraelAbolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform)That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country.The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it.I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:71% of Americans reject socialism67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialismBut here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth.**[I'm standing up to them.](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/qOvOd2DB2hLb1tDeeiiK6Mj1sDJELZgJ7wEgMy_wdWaxIVIsSVDgDA64X_yFh9QlbKfsOGNEqI7nDUVOjXtNKFUe5yZ2lhuL0Uzgg19kc8QedsLo6GGqGsU44uYOB_lZsOHnCj_eeO868eFcmA2szXPsLZ1kutpQsptdRdnnYs56BJaJ0fKFTmnvhL86jLdarmuxHyfwBV3CmCaZJbLg1G6TljOV6QxNdjgmzKReU041wSlvQAFXX5D5-Kk_kMpxE474vSxVNXIrOl1jRwY_7j7RqBOtNcrOrN_csMCxEAhfHU0G2oz1r1aOgLlRsp6r80o2dkdOwn6LPeSZswT1b_LWGLP9pxhlUB7NgyAjybVtRL7Ve657j5YNrpvi4cwJGwWU0SMUM_CakGPF7jTiQxX_etNEW19xqvr7FPL5IjiJxgTwugIQi9lLToEo14KRz-WEPe8S5f0yy0jvbthY-CFygiO76_Xu1vBwsdtPx9cYLMgOKwEScfvOo_Pli8UkN6vKGRLFNrp8SUrYQxH3KfpaHqar9XGaFnx84WnQNhIf8ooZznN0dzxm4JE5uaxYnupt9elG6f7RGQS7ZEvB2a7HuKy6PRBPTffddkBuycKRbwM8PFqlx87vYZZt_tOKd52ZsggMykCeDeHo2ay1GGgYMnLd2YzOs4SUCV4YHlrfRuuHB91TKH4z-4vEmkFK6SvQkd6fT6WvSMGQT4eO6vsqTS-dggXA-i9QlUgQfAitxhStQck70rqEbPwq5-dzmkZfcO4pgQYilN2HLu1YIM-1ZJcZVvlC1Yb4ZiRy7jz94IAYPvyLoaHdixG86AtEUVOu8DKeCfrw_M9AcdG6YrBh5yCptiO5gqygz04NdtEe4nvg_fEyvfg/iLePya3LU3fe02VpO9xivFkSv5UmUVx6/25)** But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? I'm always going to reject Socialism.I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to...Abolish our bordersAbolish the electoral collegeAbolish IsraelAbolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform)That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country.The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it.I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:71% of Americans reject socialism67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialismBut here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth. But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me: "Fetterman Draws Shadow Primary From Democrats Eager to Replace Him: The Pennsylvania senator has long irked members of his own party" ~ Bloomberg If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense and putting our country first.Thank you!John Fetterman P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). Friend, there’s one question people ask me at every campaign stop: “Are you liberal or conservative?”
My answer, every time, is “Yes, of course.”
When I say that, people almost always stare at me for a second, and then they blurt out, “No, no, _which are you?_ ”
I get why they’re asking. In these deeply divided times, people put a lot of stock in how we label ourselves politically. If someone identifies as liberal, people think they know what that person stands for. Same if someone defines themselves as conservative. But like I tell the people who ask me which I am: **_I think we can — and must — be both._**
**To be liberal can mean to be generous of spirit, open to reform and able to see things with fresh eyes. To be conservative can mean holding on to values and beliefs that are really important.**
Those are both important perspectives to bring to the table — and I think at some level, we all know we are not 100% one or the other all of the time. Maybe you think of yourself as an incredibly liberal person. I bet you’re still conservative compared to _someone_ you know. And if you identify as deeply conservative — well, I bet you can still think of someone that _you’re_ liberal compared to.
That’s why I don’t focus on the political label. I think what matters far more is whether you stand up for your neighbors and your community. And after talking to thousands of people throughout the state, I think Kansans agree with me. That’s probably why I’ve had more people than I can count come up to me and say, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat, but I’m going to vote for you.”
**Friend, this might not be a typical approach to politics, but I believe it’s resonating with voters. It’s why we’re narrowly leading in the polls and Roger Marshall and his allies are spending big to slow us down. Case File No DRT-ED-LIGHT · Special File · The Speed of Light
The Next AI Bottleneck Isn’t the Chip. It’s the Wire — and the Money Is Moving to Light.
While the world argued about an AI bubble, Nvidia quietly committed billions to companies that move data with light instead of copper. Here’s why the biggest player in AI is betting on photonics, and why most investors haven’t noticed.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Most of the AI debate is about chips: who makes the fastest GPU, who gets the next shipment. But inside the world’s biggest data centers, engineers are fighting a different battle. The problem is no longer how fast a chip can think. It’s how fast thousands of chips can talk to each other. The answer the industry is betting on is light.
The bottleneck
| | Why Copper Is Running Out of Road
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Today, most signals inside AI systems travel over copper. As data rates climb, copper loses signal quality and burns more power. It still works inside a single server rack, but it struggles across multiple racks. Nvidia’s planned Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 links 576 GPUs across eight racks: copper inside the racks, optical links between them.
| OUR THEORY
---
Every leap in AI model size means more chips working as one machine. That machine is only as fast as its slowest connection. Once the connections become the limit, whoever controls the fastest, coolest-running links controls the next phase of the buildout.
Follow the money
| | Where the Smart Money Has Already Moved
---|---

---
| Lumentum$2 billion from NvidiaSame week. Lasers and optical modules.
---
| Marvell$2 billion from NvidiaChips that drive optical data links.
---

---
| Ayar LabsPart of a $500 million roundIts co-packaged optics module is expected to begin sampling in late 2026 at 6.4 terabits per second.
---
| EVIDENCE
---
Altogether, Nvidia has committed roughly $6.5 billion or more to photonics since March, on top of the optical switching platforms it introduced in 2025 with TSMC, Coherent, Lumentum, Corning and Foxconn.
Decoder
| | What a Chipmaker Buying Light Really Means
---|---

---|---
What it says
AI clusters are getting too big for copper.
What it means
**Our theory:** the world’s most valuable chip company doesn’t write multibillion-dollar checks for a side project. It writes them for a bottleneck it can’t afford to have. When the leader starts funding its suppliers’ factories, it’s telling you where the next shortage is.
Winners & losers
| | Who Gains if Light Replaces Copper
---|---
| | WINNING
---
Optical component makers
Lasers, modulators and optical engines move from niche parts to core infrastructure.
| | WINNING
---

More links between racks means far more fiber inside every data center.
| | WATCH
---
Copper-based connectivity
Still dominant inside racks, but losing the longer links as clusters grow.
| | WINNING
---
Power-hungry data centers
Optical links use less energy per bit, and energy is now AI’s other bottleneck.
| ClassificationTransition
---
This is a shift in AI’s architecture. The first wave rewarded the companies making the brains. The next one may reward the companies making the nervous system. The big money has moved, and most investors are still watching the chips.

---
|
---

That makes the companies building those links one of the most direct ways into AI’s next wave.

If the links between GPUs can’t keep up, Nvidia’s customers can’t use all the computing power they paid for, and they stop buying more. Our theory: by funding the optical supply chain, Nvidia is protecting its own growth. That makes the companies building those links one of the most direct ways into AI’s next wave. | | (ad by Millionaire Media) | | | At Deep Regime Trends, we write for people who think for themselves. ##### Republicans had a slightly less terrible week, and you can bet they'll spin it as a turnaround. [Matt Robison](https://open.substack.com/users/13271771-matt-robison?utm_source=mentions) has the numbers that say otherwise: Trump at 37.7 percent approval in the Silver Bulletin average, a generic ballot heading toward D+8, and consumer sentiment at its second-lowest reading on record.
##### Matt lays out the three reasons he expects this to be a sucker's rally, where the Republican ad money is actually going, and why the Susan Collins race in Maine is the one to watch right now.

* * *
### Toplines for the Week
When bear markets rally, financial experts like to say that "even a dead cat will bounce if it falls far enough and fast enough." Well, things got so bad for Republicans last week that when they got a few tenths of a percent better on some key indicators in recent days, it counted as good news, even if it's probably just a levitating deceased feline.
Is that enough to say they "won" the week? Well, from the standpoint of intellectual consistency, it is fair to say so, since the numbers were better for Republicans than they were a week ago, even if it's by the merest statistical whisper (even though the major generic ballot averages are converging toward an 8+ point Democratic lead, which is a big deal).
The take-home is that the last seven days were like the Lord of the Rings moment where Gandalf says the air is a little bit less foul over here: Republicans are still trapped in a deep, dark hole, but it felt a tad less dank. Will that last? See below......

On Thursday, Lawrence O’Donnell played our new ad on national TV.

If you’re wondering what the heck he’s talking about, you’re not alone. This is a U.S. Senator whose job is to represent you. clean_body: Our new ad shows Ohioans exactly who Jon Husted is. His crypto friends don’t like it. | | | = Hi, On Thursday, Lawrence O’Donnell played our new ad on national TV. It’s a simple message: Jon Husted says Ohio’s jobs will be replaced by robots as if it's a foregone conclusion – and, even worse: that it’s “not a bad thing.” If you’re wondering what the heck he’s talking about, you’re not alone. This is a U.S. Senator whose job is to represent you. Instead he’s representing his big tech friends, crypto insiders, and even the infamous Winklevoss twins – who I have doubts have ever stepped in Ohio, and who definitely don’t give a damn about any of our jobs or what happens to them. And tonight – just a week after we learned crypto is throwing in another $30 million to try to stop Ohio voters from recognizing what’s becoming obvious when you look at what Husted says and does – President Trump is coming to Ohio to stump for Washington’s golden boy. Republicans are lining up to bail out Jon Husted, because they know he’s so out of touch with the people of Ohio, and so willing to do their bidding. = What comes through in our ad is Jon Husted doesn’t listen to people, and he doesn’t care about people. It’s all right there in his own words. What about what he does? Well, he votes to cut taxes for billionaires. He’s voted 14 times for the war in Iran, and we’re seeing diesel prices and fertilizer prices and gas prices and food prices go up and up and up. The editor of the largest newspaper in Ohio called him the point person responsible for $2.5 billion dollars in tax breaks for the data centers coming into our state. It’s shameful. If you agree with the message in our new ad, I need your help to get it out to more undecided voters across Ohio, or those who may need a little more motivation to get out and vote. We’ve got to keep sharing our message, and to do that, I’m going to need your help. = I appreciate anything you can do and trust you to make that call. I’ll be on the other side doing everything I can to fight for you and win this race. Thank you. Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

subject: Here’s what to expect at our debate
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2045%2E1086043%2EQOHYh5)
Peter, it’s Wes.
**I'm gearing up to debate my opponent, Dan Cox, on Tuesday night.**
Here’s what to expect: when we get on that stage, Dan Cox will attack my record. That’s all he’s been doing for months.
So let's talk about that record.
Together in Maryland, we raised the minimum wage. We lowered taxes for the middle class. We delivered paid family and medical leave, and cut red tape for small businesses.
Our kids' math and reading scores are rising, and violent crime has hit its lowest level in decades.
We’ve brought jobs and new housing to our state, and strengthened community safety efforts in every neighborhood.
So when we're standing on that stage, Peter, the choice will be clear.
_Do Marylanders want to keep moving forward, or lose all the progress we've made?_
I know which side I'm on. If you’re with me, I’m asking you to show your support before I walk onto that stage, so we can reach voters who haven’t decided.

name: Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund
subject: A 20-year NYPD hero is facing life in prison
body:
Never in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like
this.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6313870/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvS2VuN2dWTTdLTg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjEwMDM/LbmNsNnZ3UzM4MQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNON29JeXZwQ2V4R3Fsc10/gasGADw/sep269c944b

Dear Friend,
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Never in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like
this.

BUT THE TRUTH IS, MY FAMILY AND I ARE OUT OF OPTIONS. AND YOU'RE OUR
ONLY HOPE.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

This is a photo of my brother, Anthony DeLustro.

Anthony spent more than 20 years serving citizens as an NYPD cop,
hunting down dangerous drug dealers and busting up drug dens.

On 9/11, he helped evacuate hundreds of people from one of the
buildings just before it collapsed. Since that day, he’s been
battling cancer and Ground Zero Lung from the toxic fumes.

We really thought Anthony had been through the worst of it.

And when he told us he was taking a police job in a small South
Carolina town so he could spend his golden years close to his
grandkids, I was so relieved.

[Image showing officer, police officer, and captain]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

[Image showing officer, police officer, and captain]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

How could I have known he was about to face the greatest danger of his
life?

I’m not talking about a drug dealer or a terrorist or even cancer...

...BUT A LOCAL PROSECUTOR HELLBENT ON DESTROYING MY BROTHER FOR
DEFENDING HIMSELF WHEN HE WAS THE VICTIM OF A ROAD RAGE INCIDENT.

Let me explain.

The day Anthony was attacked, he was off duty. He and his wife had
stopped for lunch after spending the morning at a “Coffee With A
Cop” community event.

And as they tried to pull out of the crowded restaurant parking lot...

...another driver, in a fit of road rage, jumped out of his car and
began screaming threats at my brother.

Anthony tried to calm him down.

But the man attacked him, striking him over and over.

My brother could see the situation was spiraling out of control. He
pulled out his badge and told the man he was under arrest.

But instead of complying...

...the man knocked the badge out of Anthony’s hand.

Then he got in his car and tried to flee, dragging my brother with his
vehicle and running over his legs.

In that moment, Anthony knew he was about to be crushed to death in
front of his own wife.

So he fired a single shot into his attacker’s arm, bringing the car
to a stop.

Anthony’s quick thinking saved his life.

But the road rage driver who attacked him died at the scene.

When I got the call that Anthony had been assaulted and was in the
hospital with serious injuries, I couldn’t believe what had
happened.

I was so relieved he was alive.

BUT MY RELIEF TURNED INTO SHOCK WHEN MY BROTHER WAS ARRESTED AND
CHARGED WITH MURDER.

He hadn’t even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor
dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail.

He’s already spent 10 months behind bars.

And he’s facing up to 30 YEARS in prison.

My friend, Anthony is 64 years old.

If he’s convicted...

...HE’LL LIKELY SPEND THE REST OF HIS LIFE LOCKED UP--AND DIE IN
PRISON--FOR DEFENDING HIMSELF.

THAT'S WHY I'M WRITING YOU--SOMEONE I'VE NEVER MET--TO ASK YOU TO HELP
MY BROTHER.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Because what they’re doing to Anthony is an outrage.

I might not be a cop...but to me, if a police officer puts you under
arrest, you don’t resist.

And you certainly don’t physically attack the officer, then try to
flee the scene.

My brother may have been off duty. But you know that as an off-duty
officer, he had the authority--and even the responsibility--to make an
arrest to protect the public.

What does this prosecutor expect off-duty officers to do--just let
angry, violent offenders beat them up, resist arrest, and then walk
away like nothing happened?

[Image showing adult, man, and person]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

My friend, Anthony doesn’t deserve this.

He’s a good man who’s well-respected by his fellow officers.

He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline.
He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations.

So to watch my brother’s life be torn apart like this is just
heartbreaking.

It’s been hard on his family too.

Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters
into their home. They’ve been raising them ever since.

You can imagine the pain it’s caused these poor girls to have their
grandfather locked up and treated like a common criminal.

My friend, we were almost out of hope.

And then we found out about the LAW ENFORCEMENT LEGAL DEFENSE FUND.

You know the LELDF is a national group that’s helped dozens of
innocent officers clear their names when they’re wrongly accused by
radical prosecutors.

And they’ve agreed to help Anthony too.

Not only are they getting my brother the legal defense he deserves --
they’re also raising money to pay for the best attorneys and expert
witnesses available.

Which brings me to the reason I wrote you today:

MY FRIEND, WILL YOU HELP MY BROTHER FIGHT THESE UNJUST CHARGES BY
DONATING TO THE LELDF?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Because the truth of it is, the legal bills are already overwhelming.
And we haven’t even gotten to trial!

Anthony and his wife have already drained almost their entire life’s
savings fighting to free him.

So any amount you can give today will help.

And because LELDF is a non-profit organization, your gift is
completely tax-deductible.

BUT WHATEVER YOU CAN AFFORD TO GIVE, I'M ASKING YOU TO PLEASE MAKE
YOUR GIFT TODAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

After the four decades serving his community, the cancer, and the
injuries from his attack, Anthony deserves to spend his retirement
years in peace with his family -- NOT locked up behind bars for the
rest of his life.

But that’s exactly what will happen unless friends like you step up
on his behalf.

Thank you for taking the time to read my email today.

THANK YOU IN ADVANCE FOR MAKING YOUR TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT TO HELP
ANTHONY FIGHT TO CLEAR HIS NAME.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

And please, keep my brother in your prayers.

_FRANK DELUSTRO_

P.S. Anthony didn’t know it at the time, but the road-rage maniac
who attacked him had a criminal record. Maybe that’s why he was so
eager to flee the scene after my brother arrested him.

PLEASE HELP SAVE ANTHONY FROM SPENDING THE REST OF HIS LIFE BEHIND
BARS. MAKE A TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT OF ANY AMOUNT TO THE LAW ENFORCEMENT
LEGAL DEFENSE FUND RIGHT AWAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

STAND WITH OFFICER DELUSTRO
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

BUT MY RELIEF TURNED INTO SHOCK WHEN MY BROTHER WAS ARRESTED AND CHARGED WITH MURDER. He hadn’t even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail. He’s already spent 10 months behind bars. And he’s facing up to 30 YEARS in prison. My friend, Anthony is 64 years old. If he’s convicted... ...HE’LL LIKELY SPEND THE REST OF HIS LIFE LOCKED UP--AND DIE IN PRISON--FOR DEFENDING HIMSELF. THAT'S WHY I'M WRITING YOU--SOMEONE I'VE NEVER MET--TO ASK YOU TO HELP MY BROTHER. [ Because what they’re doing to Anthony is an outrage. I might not be a cop...but to me, if a police officer puts you under arrest, you don’t resist. And you certainly don’t physically attack the officer, then try to flee the scene. My brother may have been off duty. But you know that as an off-duty officer, he had the authority--and even the responsibility--to make an arrest to protect the public. What does this prosecutor expect off-duty officers to do--just let angry, violent offenders beat them up, resist arrest, and then walk away like nothing happened? [Image showing adult, man, and person] [ My friend, Anthony doesn’t deserve this. He’s a good man who’s well-respected by his fellow officers. He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline. He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations. So to watch my brother’s life be torn apart like this is just heartbreaking. It’s been hard on his family too. Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters into their home. They’ve been raising them ever since. You can imagine the pain it’s caused these poor girls to have their grandfather locked up and treated like a common criminal. My friend, we were almost out of hope. And then we found out about the LAW ENFORCEMENT LEGAL DEFENSE FUND. You know the LELDF is a national group that’s helped dozens of innocent officers clear their names when they’re wrongly accused by radical prosecutors. And they’ve agreed to help Anthony too. Not only are they getting my brother the legal defense he deserves -- they’re also raising money to pay for the best attorneys and expert witnesses available. Which brings me to the reason I wrote you today: MY FRIEND, WILL YOU HELP MY BROTHER FIGHT THESE UNJUST CHARGES BY DONATING TO THE LELDF? [ Because the truth of it is, the legal bills are already overwhelming. And we haven’t even gotten to trial! Anthony and his wife have already drained almost their entire life’s savings fighting to free him. So any amount you can give today will help. And because LELDF is a non-profit organization, your gift is completely tax-deductible. BUT WHATEVER YOU CAN AFFORD TO GIVE, I'M ASKING YOU TO PLEASE MAKE YOUR GIFT TODAY. [ After the four decades serving his community, the cancer, and the injuries from his attack, Anthony deserves to spend his retirement years in peace with his family -- NOT locked up behind bars for the rest of his life. But that’s exactly what will happen unless friends like you step up on his behalf. Thank you for taking the time to read my email today. THANK YOU IN ADVANCE FOR MAKING YOUR TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT TO HELP ANTHONY FIGHT TO CLEAR HIS NAME. [ And please, keep my brother in your prayers. FRANK DELUSTRO P.S. Anthony didn’t know it at the time, but the road-rage maniac who attacked him had a criminal record. Maybe that’s why he was so eager to flee the scene after my brother arrested him. Friend — It’s hard to believe October is already here — and even harder to believe we are now just **one month away from Election Day.** _I know how quickly these final weeks can fly by._ And right now, more and more people across New Mexico and around the country are just starting to tune in. That means we have to keep showing up, reaching people where they are, sharing the facts, and making sure misinformation doesn’t reach them before we do. Serving New Mexico has been the honor of my life. From my time on the Albuquerque City Council, to helping flip the 1st Congressional District blue for the first time, to serving in the Senate today, I’ve always believed that public service is about building a better future for the people who call this state home. **That’s why I’ve worked to make life more affordable for New Mexico families, build our clean energy economy, create good-paying jobs, and protect the public lands that belong to all of us.** And this election will help determine whether we can keep making progress. **We need to elect Democrats who will work for you, not bend the knee to a corrupt administration.** That’s why we need to support Democrats throughout New Mexico, protect Senate Democrats, and flip at least four red seats blue. There’s a lot we need to accomplish in the month ahead. But I’m grateful to be doing this alongside you — _and I’m proud of what we can accomplish together._ Thank you, Martin
